posts.title: The Download: Pelosi’s successor targets AI and data centers face power woes
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI —Grace Huckins As a California state senator, Scott Wiener authored legislation aimed at curbing the risks of advanced AI. Now, after winning a…
bullets: Scott Wiener, the successor to Nancy Pelosi’s congressional seat, is positioning himself as a key federal advocate for strict AI regulation, specifically targeting the risks of recursive self-improvement.

The rapid expansion of data centers is facing significant public and political backlash, which analysts suggest is fundamentally driven by the industry's massive and unsustainable appetite for electricity.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is under FBI investigation regarding an affair, a development that is already fueling speculation about potential new chip export restrictions and impacts on China-related lobbying.
The convergence of AI policy shifts and potential instability in the semiconductor leadership sector poses a material threat to broader economic stability and tech-sector market valuations.

posts.title: Test Struggles To Keep Pace With AI
posts.summary:
Rapidly changing workloads, more test insertions, and fragmented data complicate chip testing.
The post Test Struggles To Keep Pace With AI appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The rapid evolution of AI algorithms means chip workloads often change between design and final test, rendering traditional deterministic testing insufficient.
Multi-die assemblies and high-performance processors now require complex multiphysics simulations and real-time monitoring of thermal gradients and signal integrity.
Testing is shifting toward the substrate level, with functional testing now being integrated into substrate inspection to handle the increased complexity of modern AI packages.

posts.title: AI’s Efficiency Challenge For The Semiconductor Industry
posts.summary:
AI is reshaping the tools, data, and collaboration models used to design, manufacture, and test silicon.
The post AI’s Efficiency Challenge For The Semiconductor Industry appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The semiconductor industry is projected to grow from $975 billion in 2025 to $2.3 trillion by 2030, with data centers accounting for 58% of that expansion.
Meeting this demand requires an estimated 9.6 to 17.5 million additional wafers annually, necessitating the construction of 16 to 29 new 50,000-wafer-per-month fabs.

Efficiency has become the primary operational focus, as manufacturers struggle to secure new equipment and must instead maximize the output of existing assets through AI-driven data and supply chain connectivity.

posts.title: Automakers' shares of China's NEV exports in October: BYD leads with 28.3%, Tesla rises to 10.1%
posts.summary:
BYD exported 164,679 NEVs in October, down 5.5% from September, with its share falling 2.8 percentage points.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD maintained its lead in China's NEV export market with a 28.3% share, despite a 5.5% month-on-month decline in export volume.
Tesla China experienced a significant recovery, with exports surging 93.3% month-on-month to capture a 10.1% market share.
Geely demonstrated strong momentum with a 488% year-on-year export increase, narrowing the gap with second-place Chery to just 0.6 percentage points.

posts.title: China NEV market share in October: BYD leads with 22.4%, Tesla drops out of top 10
posts.summary:
Xiaomi rose to sixth, while GWM and Xpeng entered the October NEV retail top 10.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD continues to dominate the domestic retail market with a 22.4% share, though its lead over second-place Geely is narrowing.
Xiaomi Auto achieved the fastest growth among top-tier players, rising to sixth place with 50,123 retail units and a 4.5% market share.
Tesla dropped out of the top 10 domestic retail rankings in October, highlighting the intense competition from domestic manufacturers like Leapmotor and Changan.
